Newton ModelBuilder Performance

Benchmarks for stale PR 1718 optimization ideas on a fresh current-main clone. The workloads load MuJoCo-menagerie-style USD assets, register the MuJoCo custom attributes, replicate them to RL-scale world counts, and measure ModelBuilder.finalize(). This version also measures repeated ModelBuilder.add_builder() calls, which is the relevant construction path for IsaacLab-style workflows.

Generated at 2026-06-05T21:52:31+00:00

Finalize scope

Timing starts after USD load and environment replication. It measures only builder.finalize(device="cuda:0") plus device synchronization, with peak host RSS sampled during the call.

add_builder scope

Timing starts and stops around each single builder.add_builder(robot_builder) call. The loop creates N worlds, records total call time, median/p95 call time, and last-call time as the destination builder grows.

PR context

PR 1718 was too far behind current main to rebase cleanly, so these are targeted runtime patches representing the optimization ideas rather than a direct benchmark of the stale branch.

Deep Finalize Diagnosis

These one-off diagnostic runs instrumented G1 16k finalize() to separate contact-pair generation, expanded collision filter pairs, custom attributes, and Warp array conversion. They are not optimization variants; they isolate cost centers.

Largest confirmed hotspot: Unitree G1 with hands has 5,518 source shape collision filter pairs when self-collisions are disabled. At 16k worlds, replicate() expands that to 90,406,912 Python filter-pair tuples. Current finalize() then normalizes them with min()/max() and inserts them into a Python set before contact generation.

The diagnostic isolate that skips contact generation but keeps the expanded filter-pair list still took 111.8s. Skipping contact generation and dropping the expanded filter-pair list took 26.0s. That makes collision-filter representation the first optimization to implement, ahead of more mesh hashing or callback cleanup.

What The Variant Names Mean

Mesh SHA hash

Low

Changes the first-time mesh hash from Python tuple hashing of every vertex/index to a SHA-256 hash over the mesh buffers. This targets large mesh hashing overhead.

add_builder(): No direct effect on add_builder(); it only changes hash calls made later by finalize().

def __hash__(self):
    cached = getattr(self, "_cached_hash", None)
    if cached is None:
        h = hashlib.sha256(self._vertices.tobytes())
        h.update(self._indices.tobytes())
        cached = int.from_bytes(h.digest()[:8], "big")
        self._cached_hash = cached
    return cached

Geometry id dedup

Low

Inside finalize(), use the geometry object's identity as the deduplication key. Replicated worlds reuse the same mesh objects, so identity avoids repeatedly hashing equivalent geometry.

add_builder(): No direct effect on add_builder(); it changes finalize()'s geometry dedup lookup.

for geo in self.shape_source:
    geo_hash = id(geo)
    if geo_hash not in finalized_geos:
        finalized_geos[geo_hash] = finalize_geometry(geo)

Custom attr wp.full

Low-Medium

When a custom attribute has no explicit values, allocate the Warp array directly with wp.full(count, default). This avoids building a huge Python list of repeated defaults before converting it.

add_builder(): No direct effect on add_builder(); it changes how finalize() materializes Model/State/Control custom attributes.

if self.values is None or len(self.values) == 0:
    if self.dtype is str:
        return [self.default] * count
    return wp.full(
        count,
        self.default,
        dtype=self.dtype,
        requires_grad=requires_grad,
        device=device,
    )

Array proxy

High

Benchmark-only proxy for the stale PR's array-backed ModelBuilder fields. It converts selected Python lists to compact array.array or NumPy storage immediately before finalize().

add_builder(): Not applied to add_builder(); converting before add_builder would change source/destination builder semantics. The add_builder plots are therefore a negative-control for this finalize-only proxy.

for name in INT_FIELDS:
    values = getattr(builder, name, None)
    if isinstance(values, list) and values:
        setattr(builder, name, array("i", (int(v) for v in values)))

for name in STRUCTURED_FLOAT_FIELDS:
    values = getattr(builder, name, None)
    if isinstance(values, list) and values:
        setattr(builder, name, np.asarray(values, dtype=np.float32))

Replicated contact-pair template

Medium

For replicated worlds, compute the contact-pair pattern for the first world and replay the same local/global pair offsets for later worlds. This avoids scanning all filtered robot-robot shape pairs in every environment.

add_builder(): No direct effect on add_builder(); it changes finalize() contact-pair construction.

first_world_pairs = build_contact_pairs_for_world(0)
for world in range(world_count):
    start = shape_world_start[world]
    for a_offset, b_offset in first_world_pairs:
        contact_pairs.append((start + a_offset, start + b_offset))

Compact collision-filter blocks

High

Store replicated shape-collision filter pairs as one local template plus one shape offset per copied world, and use that compact metadata to build contact pairs. This avoids creating and then canonicalizing tens of millions of Python tuples for large replicated robots.

add_builder(): Direct add_builder()/replicate() optimization for filtered USD robots, and a direct finalize() optimization because the giant filter set is no longer materialized.

local_filter_pairs = tuple(source.shape_collision_filter_pairs)
builder.shape_collision_filter_pairs.extend_offset(local_filter_pairs, start_shape_idx)

if filter_blocks_cover_all_pairs:
    model.shape_collision_filter_pairs = LazyFilterView(builder.shape_collision_filter_pairs)
    find_shape_contact_pairs_from_filter_blocks(model)

add_builder bulk shape copy

Low-Medium

When add_builder() is called without a transform, copy shape body indices and shape transforms in bulk instead of looping shape-by-shape through the transform-aware path.

add_builder(): Direct add_builder() optimization for the no-transform replication path.

if xform is None:
    self.shape_body.extend([b + start_body_idx if b > -1 else -1 for b in builder.shape_body])
    self.shape_transform.extend(builder.shape_transform)
else:
    copy_shapes_with_transform(builder, xform)

add_builder batched custom attrs

Medium

Avoid per-value callback dispatch for custom attributes that are copied unchanged, and use list fills for attributes that simply become the current world index.

add_builder(): Direct add_builder() optimization for SolverMuJoCo custom-attribute-heavy builders.

if custom_value_transform_kind == "copy":
    merged.values.extend(attr.values)
elif custom_value_transform_kind == "world":
    merged.values.extend([self.current_world] * len(attr.values))

add_builder lazy transform helper

Low

Only bind the Warp transform multiplication helper when add_builder() is actually called with a transform.

add_builder(): Small direct add_builder() cleanup for the common xform=None path.

if xform is not None:
    transform_mul_cfunc = wp._src.context.runtime.core.wp_builtin_mul_transformf_transformf
    def transform_mul(a, b):
        ...
else:
    transform_mul = None

add_builder attr pair cache

Medium

Cache source/destination list pairs for the large repeated attribute-copy block in add_builder(), skipping empty source lists.

add_builder(): Direct add_builder() optimization; more intrusive because it adds cache state keyed by source builder identity.

src_cache = tuple((attr, builder_dict[attr]) for attr in ATTRS if builder_dict[attr])
dst_srcs = tuple((self_dict[attr], src) for attr, src in src_cache)
for dst, src in dst_srcs:
    dst.extend(src)

Custom attr sparse fill

Medium

Build default-filled custom-attribute arrays first, then write only explicit overrides. This targets sparse non-empty custom attributes.

add_builder(): No direct effect on add_builder(); it changes finalize() custom-attribute materialization.

arr = [self.default] * count
for i, value in values.items():
    if 0 <= i < count:
        arr[i] = value
return wp.array(arr, dtype=self.dtype, device=device)

Custom attr NumPy sparse fill

Medium

Use NumPy default-filled scalar arrays for sparse numeric custom attributes before handing them to Warp.

add_builder(): No direct effect on add_builder(); it changes finalize() custom-attribute materialization for scalar dtypes.

arr_np = np.full(count, self.default, dtype=np_dtype)
for i, value in values.items():
    arr_np[i] = value
return wp.array(arr_np, dtype=self.dtype, device=device)

add_builder Deep Dive

The table below uses the current-main baseline at the largest world count. Total add_builder s is the sum of N individually timed add_builder() calls. The first/last and head/tail columns show whether a single call gets more expensive as the destination builder grows.

add_builder baseline: at 16k worlds, current main ranges from 5.922 s total for UR5e arm to 36.385 s total for Unitree G1 with hands. The heaviest scenario has a median single-call cost of 1.475 ms and a p95 of 2.103 ms.

Growth shape: for the heaviest 16k case, the last 10% of calls average 0.927x the first 10%. That makes add_builder() a real construction-time scaling target even when finalize() is optimized.

Variant spread: the largest 16k add_builder spread across measured variants is 249.020%. Large spreads are useful prioritization signals, but the one-repeat exploratory matrix should still be followed by repeated IsaacLab-trace measurements before landing invasive changes.

Analysis

Finalize: the G1 16k diagnosis showed that expanded collision-filter pairs, not raw contact-pair enumeration, were the decisive bottleneck. Compact collision-filter blocks keeps the replicated filter template compact and lets finalize() build contact pairs from per-world templates instead of materializing a 90M-pair set. The remaining high-count cost is mostly Warp/Python array conversion and MuJoCo custom attributes.

add_builder: compact filter blocks also address the largest add_builder-specific memory problem for filtered USD robots. The older batching and bulk-shape variants remain useful secondary candidates, but their value should be judged against the new compact-filter baseline.

Recommendation

Do not port PR 1718 wholesale. The next serious patch should focus on compact collision-filter blocks because it targets the measured G1 16k bottleneck directly and helps both add_builder() and finalize(). Land it only with fallback tests for direct/global filters and heterogeneous worlds. After that, evaluate Custom attr wp.full and add_builder custom-attribute batching as separate smaller patches.

Failures

No failed benchmark cases were recorded.
